ocr_errors.ocr: Recipe et electi uncias 4: … adde inue et electi ut suus uncias 8
ocr_errors.image: ℞ ♁ii electi uncias 4: … adde iniice ♂is electi ut sit uncias 8
ocr_errors.problem: antimony and iron signs both reduced to 'et': the recipe no longer says what is weighed
the key distinction (essentially vs accidentally poisoned) is misread

ocr_errors.ocr: Rege nostri … attamen suui federe nondum luit
ocr_errors.image: Reguli noēi … attamen sui fidere nondum licet
ocr_errors.problem: several misreads

ocr_errors.ocr: Mars em arsenicale et et radicitus eliminal
ocr_errors.problem: symbols collapsed to 'et' throughout the paragraph
nitre sign and 'sicato' lost

book_verdict: Not usable: the alchemical signs are turned into plausible-looking Latin words ('spiritu', 'gem', 'Olei', 'et'), negations are invented ('non enim', 'non solventis Ursi'), recipes lose their ingredients, and p.232 appends a fake second column read from the facing leaf.

book_verdict: The best of the four: close, word-by-word readings that keep the signs, mark doubt with <unclear>, tag the pencil note as a later hand and leave out the facing-leaf strip; a few signs are dropped or misidentified, and arrow/markdown heading markup leaks into the reader text.
